definition: Two pointers scan a sequence with two indexes that move according to a rule, instead of a nested loop over every pair. On a sorted array they often start at opposite ends and move inward. Each step discards a whole set of pairs that cannot be the answer.

complexity.time: Often O(n) after the input is sorted, or O(n) on an already ordered sequence.
complexity.space: O(1) extra space besides the input.

examples: Finding two numbers in a sorted array that add up to a target
Checking whether a string is a palindrome from the outside inward
